title: अध्याय १३१

items.text:
अथैकत्रिंशदधिकशततमोऽध्यायः
दमचरितवर्णनम्
items.tr:
athaikatriṃśadadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ
damacaritavarṇanam

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
स तां लब्ध्वा तथा पत्नीं सुमनां सुमहामुने ।
प्रणम्य स पितुः पादौ मातुश्च क्षितिपात्मजः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
sa tāṃ labdhvā tathā patnīṃ sumanāṃ sumahāmune |
praṇamya sa pituḥ pādau mātuśca kṣitipātmajaḥ || 1 ||

items.text:
सा च तौ श्वशुरौ सूभ्रूर्ननाम सुमना तदा ।
ताभ्यां तौ च तदा विप्र आशीर्भिरभिनन्दितौ ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
sā ca tau śvaśurau sūbhrūrnanāma sumanā tadā |
tābhyāṃ tau ca tadā vipra āśīrbhirabhinanditau || 2 ||

items.text:
महोत्सवश्च सञ्जज्ञे नरिष्यन्तस्य वै पुरे ।
कृतदारे च सम्प्राप्ते दशार्णाधिपतेः पुरात् ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
mahotsavaśca sañjajñe nariṣyantasya vai pure |
kṛtadāre ca samprāpte daśārṇādhipateḥ purāt || 3 ||

items.text:
सम्बन्धिनं दशार्णेशं जितांश्च पृथिवीश्वरान् ।
श्रुत्या पुत्रेण मुमुदे नरिष्यन्तो महीपतिः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
sambandhinaṃ daśārṇeśaṃ jitāṃśca pṛthivīśvarān |
śrutyā putreṇa mumude nariṣyanto mahīpatiḥ || 4 ||

items.text:
सोऽपि रेमे सुमनया महाराजसुतो दमः ।
वरोद्यानवनोद्देशे प्रसादगिरिसानुषु ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
so'pi reme sumanayā mahārājasuto damaḥ |
varodyānavanoddeśe prasādagirisānuṣu || 5 ||

items.text:
अथ कालेन महता रममाणा दमेन सा ।
अवाप गर्भे सुमना दशार्णाधिपतेः सुता ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
atha kālena mahatā ramamāṇā damena sā |
avāpa garbhe sumanā daśārṇādhipateḥ sutā || 6 ||

items.text:
सोऽपि राजा नरिष्यन्तो भुक्तभोगो महीपतिः ।
वयः परिणतिं प्राप्य दमं राज्येऽभिषिच्य च ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
so'pi rājā nariṣyanto bhuktabhogo mahīpatiḥ |
vayaḥ pariṇatiṃ prāpya damaṃ rājye'bhiṣicya ca || 7 ||

items.text:
वनं जगामेन्द्रसेना पत्नी चास्य तपस्विनी ।
वानप्रस्थविधानेन स तत्र समतिष्ठत ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
vanaṃ jagāmendrasenā patnī cāsya tapasvinī |
vānaprasthavidhānena sa tatra samatiṣṭhata || 8 ||

items.text:
दाक्षिणात्यः सुदुर्वृत्तः संक्रन्दनसुतो वने ।
वपुष्मान्स मृगान्हन्तुं ययावल्पपदानुगः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
dākṣiṇātyaḥ sudurvṛttaḥ saṃkrandanasuto vane |
vapuṣmānsa mṛgānhantuṃ yayāvalpapadānugaḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
स तं दृष्ट्वा नरिष्यन्तं तापसं मलपङ्किनम् ।
इन्द्रसेनां च तत्पत्नीं तपसातिसुदुर्बलाम् ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā nariṣyantaṃ tāpasaṃ malapaṅkinam |
indrasenāṃ ca tatpatnīṃ tapasātisudurbalām || 10 ||

items.text:
पप्रच्छ कस्त्वं भो विप्रः क्षत्रियो वा वनेचरः ।
वानप्रस्थमनुप्राप्तो वैश्यो वा मम कथ्यताम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
papraccha kastvaṃ bho vipraḥ kṣatriyo vā vanecaraḥ |
vānaprasthamanuprāpto vaiśyo vā mama kathyatām || 11 ||

items.text:
ततो मौनव्रती भूपो नहि तस्योत्तरं ददौ ।
इन्द्रसेना च तत्सर्वमाचष्टास्मै यथातथम् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
tato maunavratī bhūpo nahi tasyottaraṃ dadau |
indrasenā ca tatsarvamācaṣṭāsmai yathātatham || 12 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
ज्ञात्वा तं च नरिष्यन्तं वपुष्मान्पितरं रिपोः ।
प्राप्तोऽसीति वदन्कोपाज्जटासु परिगृह्य च ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
jñātvā taṃ ca nariṣyantaṃ vapuṣmānpitaraṃ ripoḥ |
prāpto'sīti vadankopājjaṭāsu parigṛhya ca || 13 ||

items.text:
हाहेति चन्द्रसेनायां रुदन्त्यां बाष्पगद्गदम् ।
चकर्ष कोपात्सङ्गं च वाक्यं चेदमुवाच ह ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
hāheti candrasenāyāṃ rudantyāṃ bāṣpagadgadam |
cakarṣa kopātsaṅgaṃ ca vākyaṃ cedamuvāca ha || 14 ||

items.text:
निर्जितः समरे येन येन मे सुमना हृता ।
दमस्य तस्य पितरं हनिष्येऽवतु तं दमः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
nirjitaḥ samare yena yena me sumanā hṛtā |
damasya tasya pitaraṃ haniṣye'vatu taṃ damaḥ || 15 ||

items.text:
येनाखिलमहीपालपुत्राः कन्यार्थमागताः ।
अवधूता हनिष्येऽहं पितरं तस्य दुर्मतेः ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
yenākhilamahīpālaputrāḥ kanyārthamāgatāḥ |
avadhūtā haniṣye'haṃ pitaraṃ tasya durmateḥ || 16 ||

items.text:
यौवनास्त्रस्वरूपेषु मदे यस्य दुरात्मनः ।
स दमो वारयत्वेष हन्मि तस्या रिपोर्गुरुम् ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
yauvanāstrasvarūpeṣu made yasya durātmanaḥ |
sa damo vārayatveṣa hanmi tasyā riporgurum || 17 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इत्युक्त्वा स दुराचारो वपुष्मानवनीपतिः ।
क्रंदन्त्यामिन्द्रसेनायां शिरश्चिच्छेद तस्य च ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
ityuktvā sa durācāro vapuṣmānavanīpatiḥ |
kraṃdantyāmindrasenāyāṃ śiraściccheda tasya ca || 18 ||

items.text:
ततो धिग्धिङ्मुनिजना अन्ये च वनवासिनः ।
तमूचुः स च तं हत्वा जगाम स्वपुरं वनात् ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
tato dhigdhiṅmunijanā anye ca vanavāsinaḥ |
tamūcuḥ sa ca taṃ hatvā jagāma svapuraṃ vanāt || 19 ||

items.text:
गते तस्मिन्विनिश्वस्य सेन्द्रसेना वपुष्मति ।
प्रेषयामास पुत्रस्य समीपं शूद्रतापसम् ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
gate tasminviniśvasya sendrasenā vapuṣmati |
preṣayāmāsa putrasya samīpaṃ śūdratāpasam || 20 ||

items.text:
गच्छेथा आशु मे पुत्रं दमं ब्रूहि वचो मम ।
अभिज्ञो ह्यसि मद्भर्तृवृत्तान्तं प्रोच्यतेऽत्र किम् ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
gacchethā āśu me putraṃ damaṃ brūhi vaco mama |
abhijño hyasi madbhartṛvṛttāntaṃ procyate'tra kim || 21 ||

items.text:
तथापि वाच्यः पुत्रो मे यद्ब्रवीम्यतिदुःखिता ।
लंघनामीदृशीं प्राप्तां विलोक्यतां महीपतेः ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
tathāpi vācyaḥ putro me yadbravīmyatiduḥkhitā |
laṃghanāmīdṛśīṃ prāptāṃ vilokyatāṃ mahīpateḥ || 22 ||

items.text:
मद्भर्त्राऽधिकृतो राजा चतुर्णां परिपालकः ।
त्वमाश्रमाणां किं युक्तं तापसान्यन्न रक्षसि ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
madbhartrā'dhikṛto rājā caturṇāṃ paripālakaḥ |
tvamāśramāṇāṃ kiṃ yuktaṃ tāpasānyanna rakṣasi || 23 ||

items.text:
भर्ता मम नरिष्यन्तस्तापसस्तपसि स्थितः ।
विलपन्त्यास्तथा नाथो यथा नासि तथा त्वयि ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
bhartā mama nariṣyantastāpasastapasi sthitaḥ |
vilapantyāstathā nātho yathā nāsi tathā tvayi || 24 ||

items.text:
आकृष्य केशेषु बलादपराधं विना ततः ।
हतो वपुष्मता ख्यातिमिति ते भूपतिर्गता ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
ākṛṣya keśeṣu balādaparādhaṃ vinā tataḥ |
hato vapuṣmatā khyātimiti te bhūpatirgatā || 25 ||

items.text:
एवं स्थिते तत्क्रियतां यथा धर्मो न लुप्यते ।
तथा च नैव वस्तव्यं माताहं तापसी यतः ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ sthite tatkriyatāṃ yathā dharmo na lupyate |
tathā ca naiva vastavyaṃ mātāhaṃ tāpasī yataḥ || 26 ||

items.text:
पिता वृद्धस्तपस्वी च नापराधेन दूषितः ।
निहतो येन यत्तस्य कर्तव्यं तद्विचिन्त्यताम् ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
pitā vṛddhastapasvī ca nāparādhena dūṣitaḥ |
nihato yena yattasya kartavyaṃ tadvicintyatām || 27 ||

items.text:
सन्ति ते मन्त्रिणो वीराः सर्वशास्त्रार्थवेदिनः ।
तैः सहालोच्य यत्कार्यमेवंभूते कुरुष्व तत् ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
santi te mantriṇo vīrāḥ sarvaśāstrārthavedinaḥ |
taiḥ sahālocya yatkāryamevaṃbhūte kuruṣva tat || 28 ||

items.text:
नास्माकमधिकारोऽत्र तापसानां नराधिप ।
कुरुष्वैतदितीत्थं त्वमेवं भूपतिभाषितम् ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
nāsmākamadhikāro'tra tāpasānāṃ narādhipa |
kuruṣvaitaditītthaṃ tvamevaṃ bhūpatibhāṣitam || 29 ||

items.text:
विदूरथस्य जनको यवनेन यथा हतः ।
तथायं तव पुत्रस्य कुलं तेन विनाशितम् ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
vidūrathasya janako yavanena yathā hataḥ |
tathāyaṃ tava putrasya kulaṃ tena vināśitam || 30 ||

items.text:
जम्भस्यासुरराजस्य पिता दष्टो भुजङ्गमैः ।
तेनाप्यखिलपातालवासिनः पन्नगाः हताः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
jambhasyāsurarājasya pitā daṣṭo bhujaṅgamaiḥ |
tenāpyakhilapātālavāsinaḥ pannagāḥ hatāḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
पराशरेण पितरं शक्तिं तं रक्षसाऽऽहतम् ।
श्रुत्वाऽग्नौ पातितं कृत्स्नं रक्षसामभवत्कुलम् ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
parāśareṇa pitaraṃ śaktiṃ taṃ rakṣasā''hatam |
śrutvā'gnau pātitaṃ kṛtsnaṃ rakṣasāmabhavatkulam || 32 ||

items.text:
अन्यस्यापि स्ववंशस्य लंघना क्रियते हि या ।
तां नालं क्षत्रियः सोढुं कि पुनः पितृमारणम् ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
anyasyāpi svavaṃśasya laṃghanā kriyate hi yā |
tāṃ nālaṃ kṣatriyaḥ soḍhuṃ ki punaḥ pitṛmāraṇam || 33 ||

items.text:
नायं पिता ते निहतो नास्मिञ्छस्त्रं निपातितम् ।
त्वामत्र निहतं मन्ये त्वयि शस्त्रं निपातितम् ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
nāyaṃ pitā te nihato nāsmiñchastraṃ nipātitam |
tvāmatra nihataṃ manye tvayi śastraṃ nipātitam || 34 ||

items.text:
बिभेत्यस्य हि कः शस्त्रं न्यस्तं येन वनौकसाम् ।
तव नृपस्य पुत्रस्य मा बिभेतु बिभेतु वा ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
bibhetyasya hi kaḥ śastraṃ nyastaṃ yena vanaukasām |
tava nṛpasya putrasya mā bibhetu bibhetu vā || 35 ||

items.text:
तवेयं लङ्घनायुक्ता यदस्मिंस्तत्समाचर ।
वपुष्मति महाराज सभृत्यज्ञातिबान्धवे ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
taveyaṃ laṅghanāyuktā yadasmiṃstatsamācara |
vapuṣmati mahārāja sabhṛtyajñātibāndhave || 36 ||

items.speaker: मार्कण्डेय उवाच
items.text:
इति संक्रान्तसन्देशमिन्द्रसेना विसृज्य तम् ।
पतिदेहमुपाश्लिष्य विवेशाग्निं मनस्विनी ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
iti saṃkrāntasandeśamindrasenā visṛjya tam |
patidehamupāśliṣya viveśāgniṃ manasvinī || 37 ||

en_summary: Markandeya continues. Dama and Sumana bowed at the feet of his father and mother and were blessed, and there was a great festival in Narishyanta's city at his return with a wife; Narishyanta rejoiced to hear from his son of his new relative, the king of Dasharna, and the defeated kings. Dama enjoyed life with Sumana in fine gardens, forests and on hills near the palace, and in time she conceived. King Narishyanta, having enjoyed life and grown old, crowned Dama and went to the forest with his wife Indrasena, living by the rules of the forest-dweller. The wicked southern prince Vapushman, son of Sankrandana, went into that forest to hunt deer with a few followers. He saw Narishyanta, an ascetic covered in dirt, and his wife Indrasena, very weak from penance, and asked whether he was a Brahmin, a kshatriya living in the forest, or a vaishya in the forest stage. The king, keeping a vow of silence, did not answer, but Indrasena told him everything truly. Learning that this was Narishyanta, father of his enemy, Vapushman cried 'I have got you', seized him by his matted hair in anger and dragged him while Indrasena (here once called Chandrasena) wept, saying: he would kill the father of Dama, who beat him in battle, took Sumana from him and drove away all the princes who had come for her; let Dama save him if he could. Then, as Indrasena cried, he cut off Narishyanta's head. The sages and other forest dwellers cried 'Shame!', and he went back to his city. After he left, Indrasena sighed and sent a shudra ascetic to her son Dama with a message: you know what happened to my husband; still I, deeply grieved, tell you to see this insult to the king. My husband made you king, protector of the four stages of life; is it right that you do not protect ascetics? My husband was an ascetic devoted to penance; as I lament, you are like one with no protector. Dragged by the hair without any fault, he was killed by Vapushman, and the king has become famous for this. In this state, do what keeps dharma from being lost; I cannot stay, since I am an ascetic. Your aged father, an ascetic with no fault, was killed; think what must be done to his killer; consult your brave ministers who know all the sciences and act; we ascetics have no right to act here. She gives examples: when Viduratha's father was killed by a Yavana, Viduratha destroyed his family; when the asura king Jambha's father was bitten by snakes, Jambha killed all the snakes of the underworld; when Parashara heard that his father Shakti had been killed by a rakshasa, he burned the whole race of rakshasas in fire. A kshatriya cannot bear an insult even to another of his line, much less his father's murder. It was not your father who was killed, not on him the weapon fell; I think it was you who were killed and on you the weapon fell. Who fears the weapons of one who has given up protecting forest dwellers? Whether the king's son fears or not, deal with Vapushman, his servants, kin and relatives as this insult deserves. Having sent this message, the brave Indrasena embraced her husband's body and entered the fire.
